fields.options:
Add this to your Print Format's HTML. Leave Anchor Text above at its default - the same value works for every template regardless of size, since size lives entirely in the HTML, not here:

<div style="width:160px; height:80px; color:#ffffff; overflow:hidden; margin:4px 0;">##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR:160x80##</div>

A plain block-level div with explicit width/height - no position:absolute, no inline-block - reliably reserves that much space in the page's normal layout flow, and the anchor text sits at its top-left by default with no extra positioning needed.

The height above is an upper bound, not a forced size. The stamp is drawn tight to however many lines are actually enabled in Settings (signer/reason/location/date/certificate serial) - with fewer lines enabled it renders shorter than the declared height, with no empty top/bottom padding added. It only uses the full declared height if the content genuinely needs that much room (shrinking the font to fit rather than overflowing). Any breathing room you want around the stamp - like the margin:4px 0; above - is yours to add in the HTML; nothing is added automatically.

The :WxH suffix is optional and detected automatically from what's actually rendered - add it in the Print Format's HTML to size that particular template; leaving it off (plain ##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR##) falls back to 160x80.

Keep the div's own width matching the number in the anchor text - height can safely be generous (it's just an upper bound now), but width is used as-is for the stamp's actual drawn width.

The stamp is drawn extending downward-right from exactly where the anchor text sits (its top-left), filling only as much of the box as its content needs. The stamp content is centered horizontally within its width automatically.

Use color:#ffffff (matching the background), not opacity:0 - some PDF engines skip painting opacity:0 text entirely, dropping it from the searchable text layer too. If the surrounding background isn't white, match this color to it instead.
